title: Agent Pay Level 1 purchase with edge verification
summary: A registered agent signs its web requests with RFC 9421 and the tag Agent-pay-auth. The CDN or merchant checks the signature against the Mastercard key directory, the agent types its agentic token into the normal card form, and the authorization runs over the existing card rails. Mastercard publishes no wire schema for the network leg.

steps.label: Signed GET with tag Agent-pay-auth
steps.detail: The agent signs each request with HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421). Signature-Input carries keyid, alg, created, expires, nonce and the tag. Mastercard's guide gives the Mastercard tag as Agent-pay-auth; its testing glossary writes agent-pay-auth. The guide's example Signature-Agent host does not resolve, so this example uses a placeholder host.

payload.content:
# Illustrative example, Agent Pay developer guides as read 2026-10-11. Values are made up.
GET /product/42 HTTP/1.1
Host: shop.example.com
Signature-Agent: "https://agent-keys.example.com/"
Signature-Input: sig1=("@authority" "@path");created=1791720000;expires=1791720480;keyid="poqkLGiymh_W0uP6PZFw-dvez3QJT5SolqXBCW38r0U";alg="ed25519";nonce="e8N7S2MFd/qrd6T2R3tdfAuuANngKI7LFtKYI/vowzk=";tag="Agent-pay-auth"
Signature: sig1=:jdq0SqOwHdyHr9+r5jw3iYZH6aNGKijYp/EstF4RQTQdi5N5YYKrD+mCT1HA1nZDsi6nJKuHxUi/5Syp3rLWBA==:

failures.condition: No Signature-Input with a scheme tag
failures.outcome: Treat as an ordinary bot and apply the non-agent bot policy

steps.label: Fetch public key for keyid
steps.detail: The verifier looks up the agent key named by keyid in the directory hosted by Mastercard. Cloudflare says each network hosts its own directory and names no Mastercard URL; the directory location is not public.

failures.condition: Key not found in the directory

steps.label: Verify window, nonce, tag, signature
steps.detail: Checks in order: created and expires bracket the current time, the nonce was not seen before, the tag is valid, the signature base is rebuilt from the covered components and the Ed25519 signature verifies.

steps.label: Forward as a trusted agent
steps.detail: The edge passes the request to the merchant site, which can now serve the agent instead of challenging it as a bot.

steps.label: Fill card form with agentic token
steps.detail: The agent types the agentic token into the standard card number, expiry and security code fields. The token looks like a card number to the merchant, so PCI scope does not change. Agents may not use a card already on file at the merchant, because the network could not then see the flow as agentic.

failures.condition: Agent uses a card on file instead of an agentic token
failures.outcome: The network cannot recognize the transaction as agentic

steps.label: Submit authorization
steps.detail: The merchant processes the payment through its existing acquirer or PSP, as for any card-not-present payment.

steps.label: Authorization request
steps.detail: The network detokenizes and checks the token limits. Stripe says agentic network tokens map to the latest funding PAN and include additional information in the authorization message for issuers; neither Stripe nor Mastercard names a data element for it.

failures.condition: Token used outside its merchant, amount or time limits

steps.label: Route to issuer
steps.detail: The issuer makes the final approve or decline decision with the additional information it receives.

steps.label: Approve or decline
steps.detail: The response returns through network and acquirer. Standard chargeback rights apply afterwards; no agent-specific reason code is published.
